analyst_view.overall: Casa Pia (16th, 8 points) host Braga (8th, 17 points) at Rio Maior on Monday night. Filipe Coelho's Casa Pia have lost all five home league games and won all their points away, no striker has scored for them since 20 September, and they were knocked out of the cup at home by Atlético CP; goalkeeper André Gomes is injured (in the numbers). Braga, under Franclim Carvalho since 22 October (5 wins, 2 draws, 1 loss), play in a more direct, vertical way, beat Vitória 2-0 in the cup and KuPS 4-0 in the Conference League on Thursday, with Pau Víctor scoring once and setting up three. This is Braga's third game in ten days with a trip to Brann next; Diário de Notícias reports midfielder Vítor Carvalho is injured and Jonas Wind needs a fitness check (one report each, neither in the numbers), while Niakaté's long absence is counted. António Nobre referees, and his low record (3.3 cards a game in 3 games) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals, 0.9 for Casa Pia and 1.7 for Braga. Casa Pia's strikers have not scored in two months and they have no home point, while Braga are in form and Pau Víctor is sharp; both are already in the ratings and recent form. Wind's fitness doubt and Vítor Carvalho's injury are from one report and matter little next to Braga's other forwards, so I stay at 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners, 5.6 for Braga after an 8.1% boost for their recent corner count, and take 6.5% off Casa Pia for their few lately. Braga will have most of the ball against a Casa Pia side that has sometimes sat deep, which is what the numbers expect, so I stay at 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards, already taking 6% off for António Nobre's low record and a little off Braga, who have been booked less than usual lately. There is no rivalry here; Casa Pia chasing a first home point could add a few fouls, but nothing in the news is strong enough to move it, so I stay at 4.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.2 shots and add 27% to Braga for a very high recent volume (114 shots in six, including a 4-0 European win). I trim a little, to about 24.4, because this is Braga's third game in ten days with a Thursday night in between, Vítor Carvalho is reported out of midfield, and a run that far above their usual level tends not to hold fully against a side defending deep.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target, 5.0 for Braga after a 6.8% boost for recent accuracy, and 3.0 for a Casa Pia side whose forwards are not scoring. My small shot trim is mostly about Braga's speculative volume, not their good chances, so I stay at 8.0.
